steps.body: Not every line cuts the curve twice. y = 2x − 1 grazes y = x²: substitution gives x² − 2x + 1 = 0 — a perfect square (x − 1)², one repeated root. Geometrically the line is TANGENT: it touches at (1, 1) and leaves. And some lines miss entirely.

explanationVariants: (x − 1)² = 0 has the single root x = 1 hit twice — one touching point, not two crossings.
A doubled root means the two intersections merged: tangency.

widget.prompt: Substituting y = 2x − 1 into y = x² gives (x − 1)² = 0. Geometrically the line…

options.label: One point of contact
options.feedback: The repeated root x = 1 is two crossings collapsed into a tangent touch at (1, 1).

options.label: Crosses at two points
options.feedback: Two crossings need two DIFFERENT roots; this square has one, doubled.

options.label: Misses the parabola
options.feedback: Missing means NO real roots — but x = 1 works: 1 = 2·1 − 1.

explanationVariants: x² = x − 3 becomes x² − x + 3 = 0 with discriminant 1 − 12 = −11 < 0: no real roots, no meetings.
The discriminant is negative, so no real x satisfies both — the line passes under the parabola.

widget.prompt: For y = x² and y = x − 3: substitution gives x² − x + 3 = 0. Compute the discriminant b² − 4ac.

commonErrors.feedback: Sign: 1 − 12 = −11. Negative discriminant is exactly what 'no crossing' looks like.

widget.fallbackFeedback: b² − 4ac with a = 1, b = −1, c = 3: 1 − 12 = −11. Negative means the line never reaches the parabola.

widget.prompt: For each line paired with y = x², compute the discriminant of the substituted quadratic and sort by meeting count.

items.label: y = x − 3
items.feedback: x² − x + 3 = 0: disc 1 − 12 = −11 < 0 — they never meet.

items.label: y = −1
items.feedback: x² + 1 = 0: disc −4 < 0 — a horizontal line below the parabola misses it entirely.

widget.missFeedback: Substitute each into x² = (line), rearrange to = 0, and read b² − 4ac: positive → two, zero → one, negative → none.
widget.successFeedback: x²−x−2 (disc 9): two. x²−2x+1 and x²−4x+4 (disc 0): tangents. x²−x+3 (disc −11) and x²+1 (disc −4): misses. The parabola never dips below y = 0, so y = −1 can't reach it.

steps.body: The discriminant-zero case, seen on the grid.

widget.prompt: c1's line y = 2x − 1 grazes y = x² exactly once. Plot the touching point.

pointErrors.feedback: On the parabola, yes — but the line reads 2·2 − 1 = 3 there; they have already separated.
On the LINE, but the parabola stands at 4 there. Touching means BOTH rules agree.

widget.missFeedback: Set them equal: x² = 2x − 1 gives (x − 1)² = 0 — the double root x = 1, y = 1.
widget.successFeedback: (1, 1): the double root made visible — one point where line and curve agree, and the discriminant said so first.

predict.prompt: y = 4x − 4 with y = x²: before computing — the discriminant of x² − 4x + 4 will be…
predict.reveal: 16 − 16 = 0: a perfect square (x − 2)², so the line is tangent at (2, 4). Discriminant zero IS tangency — the same number that counted a quadratic's roots now counts a system's meetings.

steps.body: So the discriminant you met in quadratics moonlights as a geometry oracle: substitute, rearrange, and b² − 4ac announces 2, 1, or 0 meetings before you solve anything. Same number, second job — that's mathematics being economical.

explanationVariants: Discriminant 25 is positive, so the substituted quadratic has two distinct roots — two crossings.
Positive b² − 4ac means two real solutions, hence two intersection points.

widget.prompt: A substituted system yields a quadratic with discriminant 25. The line and parabola…

options.label: Cross at two points
options.feedback: Positive discriminant, two distinct real roots, two meetings — and √25 = 5 will even appear in them.

options.label: Never meet
options.feedback: Never meeting demands a NEGATIVE discriminant.

explanationVariants: x² = 2x + c has discriminant 4 + 4c; tangency needs 4 + 4c = 0, so c = −1.
x² − 2x − c = 0 is a perfect square exactly when c = −1, giving (x − 1)².
hints: Substitute: x² − 2x − c = 0. Write its discriminant in terms of c.

widget.prompt: For which c is the line y = 2x + c TANGENT to y = x²?

commonErrors.feedback: c = 1 gives discriminant 8 > 0 — two crossings. Tangency needs 4 + 4c = 0.
c = 0 gives discriminant 4 — still two meetings; go lower.
That overshoots: discriminant 4 − 8 < 0 means the line now MISSES.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Tangency needs discriminant zero: x² − 2x − c = 0 has disc 4 + 4c, which vanishes at c = −1.

takeaways: A line meets a parabola 0, 1, or 2 times.
Substitute, rearrange, read b² − 4ac: −, 0, + in that order.
Discriminant zero is tangency — merged crossings.
steps.teaser: next: the curve becomes a circle, and Pythagoras joins the system.
